Some read it with the accent on the penult

The comparative degree of the adjective πολύς [much] is πλείων [more] and in the neuter πλέον [more]. The Attics, although they very often said πλέον [more] for πλεῖον [more] and not rarely admitted the simple vowel in the trisyllabic cases πλέονος [of more], πλέονι [to more] and the rest, nevertheless in the nominative πλείων [more] and the contracted forms πλείω [more] and πλείους [more] preferred the diphthong: which Reisig, Coni. in Aristoph. p. 43, rightly observing, Elmsley on Eur. Med. 88 ought not to have opposed. For the fact that the tragedians are commonly believed to have sometimes said πλέων [more], πλέω [more], πλέους [more] rests partly on the errors of critics, partly on the faulty writing of the manuscripts. Thus three times the mistake is made in Aeschylus,
This man is wounded by the net
There is no escape, strangers, in time
